traceability.notes:
The story 026.0-DEV-ELSE-IF-ANNOTATION-POSITION is not implemented.
Key unmet acceptance criteria and requirements:
1. **Before-Else and After-Condition Positions (REQ-DUAL-POSITION-DETECTION-ELSE-IF, REQ-FALLBACK-LOGIC-ELSE-IF, REQ-POSITION-PRIORITY-ELSE-IF)** - The helper gatherBranchCommentText only inspects comments *before* the node for IfStatement branches. It has dual-position logic only for CatchClause (before vs inside body) and special line-scanning for SwitchCase; there is no analogous logic for else-if. - There is no detection of whether an IfStatement is part of an else-if chain via parent.alternate === node, and no code that looks for comments between 'else if (condition)' and the statement body. - Therefore, annotations placed after the else-if condition (the Prettier-wrapped position) will not be detected, and there is no priority resolution when annotations appear in both positions.
2. **Prettier Compatibility & Auto-Fix (REQ-PRETTIER-AUTOFIX-ELSE-IF)** - getBranchAnnotationInfo and reportMissingStory/reportMissingReq compute insert positions for all non-CatchClause branches as the start of the branch line. This causes auto-fix to insert annotations above 'if (condition)', not between condition and body for else-if. - There is no logic to detect wrapped else-if lines or to choose a Prettier-stable insertion point for else-if branches. - No tests cover Prettier-formatted else-if code or verify that auto-fix output remains stable under Prettier reformatting.
3. **Testing & Traceability** - No tests reference Story 026.0 or its requirement IDs (e.g., REQ-DUAL-POSITION-DETECTION-ELSE-IF, REQ-PRETTIER-AUTOFIX-ELSE-IF). - The require-branch-annotation test suite includes only simple 'if' examples and does not include any 'else if' constructs, comments positioned before 'else', or comments between condition and body. - There is no integration test with actual Prettier-formatted else-if code, as called for in the Definition of Done.
4. **Documentation** - Aside from the story file itself, documentation does not explain else-if annotation positions or Prettier compatibility for else-if. The rule docs still only describe generic branch annotation behavior.
Because the implementation and tests still only support the existing branch types and catch dual-position behavior (Story 025.0), and there is no special handling or testing for else-if annotation positions, the story’s acceptance criteria and requirements are not satisfied. Thus the status for this story is FAILED.
